note.title: waf & cdn detection
note.intro: identificar waf e cdn antes de qualquer recon ativo. scanear portas atraves de cloudflare produz ruido gigante e dados falsos. o alvo real ta atras do proxy. sem saber o que ta na frente, tu perde tempo e queima pelego.
sections: 2. dns lookup — o cdn check mais confiavel
commands:
# cloudflare, akamai, sucuri deixam assinaturas nos headers
curl -sI https://alvo.com | grep -iE "server:|cf-ray:|x-sucuri-id:|x-akamai-transformed:|x-cdn:"

# cloudflare
curl -sI https://alvo.com | grep -i "cf-ray"
# akamai
curl -sI https://alvo.com | grep -i "x-akamai"
# sucuri
curl -sI https://alvo.com | grep -i "x-sucuri-id"
# incapsula
curl -sI https://alvo.com | grep -i "incap_ses"
# fastly
curl -sI https://alvo.com | grep -i "fastly"

wafw00f https://alvo.com
wafw00f -l  # lista wafs suportados
wafw00f -a https://alvo.com  # agressivo, testa mais payloads

# resolver o dominio e ver se aponta pra cdn
dig A alvo.com +short
dig AAAA alvo.com +short

# cloudflare ranges
dig A alvo.com +short | grep -E "104\.|172\.6[4-9]\.|172\.7[0-1]\."

# verificar cnames
dig CNAME www.alvo.com +short
# se resolver pra *.cloudfront.net, *.akamaiedge.net, *.edgekey.net -> tem cdn

# tool dedicada
cdncheck -d alvo.com
# ou via projectdiscovery
echo "alvo.com" | cdncheck

# subdominios internos frequentemente apontam direto pro origin (sem cdn)
subfinder -d alvo.com -all -silent | dnsx -silent -a -resp | grep -v -E "cloudflare|akamai|cloudfront"

# staging/dev/correio costumam nao ter cdn
dig A mail.alvo.com +short
dig A cpanel.alvo.com +short
dig A direct.alvo.com +short
dig A origin.alvo.com +short
dig A test.alvo.com +short

# securitytrails (historico de ip)
curl -s "https://api.securitytrails.com/v1/history/alvo.com/dns/a" \
  -H "APIKEY: $ST_KEY" | jq -r '.records[].values[].ip' | sort -u

# viewdns
curl -s "https://viewdns.info/iphistory/?domain=alvo.com" | grep -oP '\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+' | sort -u

# rapiddns
curl -s "https://rapiddns.io/s/alvo.com" | grep -oP '\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+' | sort -u

# shodan via cert
# ir em https://www.shodan.io/search?query=ssl:"alvo.com"
# ou via cli
shodan search ssl:"alvo.com" --fields ip_str,org

# hash do favicon
python3 -c "
import mmh3, requests, codecs
r = requests.get('https://alvo.com/favicon.ico')
favicon = codecs.encode(r.content, 'base64')
hash = mmh3.hash(favicon)
print(hash)
"

# buscar no shodan pelo hash
# https://www.shodan.io/search?query=http.favicon.hash:<hash>
shodan search "http.favicon.hash:<hash>" --fields ip_str,org

# se servir o site -> e o origin
curl -s -H "Host: alvo.com" http://<origin_ip> -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}\n"

# comparar com o site via cdn
curl -s https://alvo.com -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}\n"

# se tamanho/ status forem parecidos -> confirmei o origin

# whatweb
whatweb -a 3 https://alvo.com

# wappalyzer cli
wappalyzer https://alvo.com

# nuclei tech-detect template
nuclei -u https://alvo.com -t ~/nuclei-templates/technologies/

# httpx tech-detect
echo "alvo.com" | httpx -tech-detect -silent

# reduzir rate limit (cloudflare bloqueia 100 req/s)
nuclei -l live.txt -rl 10 -c 15  # rate limit 10 req/s, 15 concorrentes

# usar metodo GET com header custom pra confundir waf
ffuf -u https://alvo.com/FUZZ -w wordlist.txt -H "X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1" -mc 200,301,302,403

# user-agent rotativo (waf bloqueia ua de scanner)
ffuf -u https://alvo.com/FUZZ -w wordlist.txt -H "User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0" -rate 20

#!/bin/bash
DOMAIN=$1
echo "[*] DNS..."
dig A "$DOMAIN" +short
echo "[*] CNAME..."
dig CNAME "www.$DOMAIN" +short
echo "[*] WAF (wafw00f)..."
wafw00f "https://$DOMAIN" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "is behind|WAF"
echo "[*] Headers..."
curl -sI "https://$DOMAIN" | grep -iE "server:|cf-|x-sucuri|x-akamai|x-cdn|incap"
echo "[*] Tech (httpx)..."
echo "$DOMAIN" | httpx -tech-detect -silent -title -status-code
echo "[*] Subdominios sem cdn..."
subfinder -d "$DOMAIN" -all -silent 2>/dev/null | dnsx -silent -a -resp 2>/dev/null | \
  grep -v -E "cloudflare|akamai|cloudfront|fastly" | head -10
warnings: identificar waf e cdn antes de qualquer recon ativo. scanear portas atraves de cloudflare produz ruido gigante e dados falsos. o alvo real ta atras do proxy. sem saber o que ta na frente, tu perde tempo e queima pelego.
checklist: DNS lookup — aponta pra range de cdn?
Subdominios verificados por ip direto (sem cdn)?
Favicon hash feito e cruzado no shodan?
Origin ip validado com host header?
Rate limit configurado nos scans se waf detectado?
paragraphs: identificar waf e cdn antes de qualquer recon ativo. scanear portas atraves de cloudflare produz ruido gigante e dados falsos. o alvo real ta atras do proxy. sem saber o que ta na frente, tu perde tempo e queima pelego.
alguns wafs customizados ou de vendors menores nao sao detectados. sempre cruzar com header inspection manual e dns lookup
cdncheck da projectdiscovery tem base atualizada de ranges de cdn, cloud e waf. prefira ele. grep manual quebra rapido
quando o alvo esta atras de cloudflare/akamai, o objetivo e achar o ip real do origin server.
muitos origins expostos em ip direto servem o mesmo favicon do site principal. hashing e cruzar no shodan costuma achar origins que nem passive dns pega
depois de achar o ip real, validar sem dns:
se tu tomar block de waf, o ip entra em blocklist. ter VPN/proxy com rotacao pronto antes. nuclei com -rl 10 e -c 15 evita 90% dos blocks
